title: Standard Demo v1 - AE/SE feedback roundtable (what resonated / what broke)
topics: Which demo scenarios land best by persona (platform/ML/security)
Talk track timing and where buyers get lost
Reliability issues: throttling (429), streaming disconnects, dashboard lag, model output variance
Console clickpath confusion (routes, rollouts, fallback policies)
What claims are safe vs what to avoid (benchmarks, pricing)
EU data residency and Private/VPC pivots
summary: Internal roundtable with AEs/SE/PMM to capture what resonates in the Standard Demo v1 and what breaks live. Team agreed the strongest moments are (1) showing measurable latency/cost levers in Console, (2) graceful fallback routing as a reliability story, and (3) a crisp Hosted-to-Dedicated/Private upgrade path. Main issues: occasional 429 throttling surprises, streaming disconnect anxiety, inconsistent model output causing "awkward silence", and confusion around the Console clickpath for routing + rollouts. Action items focus on tightening demo-tenant defaults, simplifying the first 5 minutes, and adding explicit Plan B steps (canned outputs + screenshots) for live failures.

transcript:
Meeting: Standard Demo v1 - AE/SE feedback roundtable (what resonated / what broke)
Recorded: 2025-01-23 17:05 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes

Attendees (Redwood): Markus Klein, Soojin Lee, Talia Benson, Renee Sullivan, Stephanie Nguyen, Lukas Meyer, Camila Reyes, Simran Kaur, Colin O'Donnell
Attendees (Internal): Avery Johnson (AE), Priyom Das (AE), Isabelle Laurent (Sales Ops/CRM), Chloe Martin (Console), Logan Wright (Telemetry), Sean Gallagher (SRE)

---
Auto Summary (Fireflies)
- Team discussed demo flow, where prospects ask questions, and common failure points.
- Most resonant segments: cost/latency controls in Console, fallback routing reliability story, deployment flexibility.
- Top issues: throttling (429), streaming disconnect risk, dashboard freshness, and inconsistent model outputs.

Topics
1. Opening narrative and timing
2. Persona branches (platform vs ML vs security)
3. Console clickpath (routes, rollouts, fallbacks)
4. Reliability + Plan B options
5. Benchmarks/pricing safe language
6. Next dry run plan

Action Items
- (see action_items field)

---
Transcript

[00:00] Markus Klein: Alright, hey everyone. This is the roundtable on the Standard Demo v1. The goal is just brutally honest feedback. What lands, what doesn’t, what broke, what made you sweat in front of a prospect.

[00:18] Talia Benson: And I’m capturing notes. If you have a specific moment, like “slide 7” or “the routing page”, say it so we can map it.

[00:25] Soojin Lee: Also, please call out language you used that felt good, or language that got you in trouble.

[00:31] Avery Johnson: I’ll start. The best moment, consistently, is when you show the cost per 1K tokens or the token breakdown dashboard and you can say, “Here is the lever, here’s the effect.” It’s tangible. People stop asking “but how” and start asking “can I do that in my VPC.”

[00:52] Stephanie Nguyen: +1. It’s the closest thing to a “wow.” But only if the dashboard updates fast enough.

[00:58] Logan Wright: Yeah, so on that. The current demo dashboards, they’re on a 60-second refresh for some panels, some are 2 minutes. Which, uh, looks like lag. We can make it more obvious it’s not broken.

[01:10] Priyom Das: The thing that breaks the vibe is when you’re narrating like “and now you’ll see the savings” and the number doesn’t move yet. People think we’re faking.

[01:20] Chloe Martin: That’s fair. We can add “last refreshed” label or a banner in the saved view.

[01:25] Markus Klein: Great. That’s a concrete fix. What about the first five minutes? Do we lose people?

[01:31] Priyom Das: Sometimes, yes. If you start in Console immediately, the platform eng folks are fine, but a VP Eng is like, “what is this product again.” I’ve been doing a 30-second setup: “We run LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, Private. You get predictable latency and cost. This tenant is preconfigured to show fallbacks, routing, and cost controls.”

[01:55] Soojin Lee: That’s good. We should bake that in as the standard opener.

[02:01] Camila Reyes: Also messaging: say “serving economics” and “reliability” early. If we wait until later, they map us to “yet another model API.”

[02:10] Lukas Meyer: In EMEA, I have to say “regions” in the first minute or it derails. They interrupt: “Where is this running? Where is data stored?”

[02:19] Markus Klein: So a short opener with deployment modes + regions + data handling, depending on persona.

[02:25] Renee Sullivan: Can I propose something? A 2-minute mini demo for Hosted only. People asked for it in Slack. Like when the call is late and you have 12 minutes.

[02:34] Stephanie Nguyen: Yes, but keep one differentiator. If it’s just “curl a chat completion,” it’s not Redwood.

[02:41] Renee Sullivan: Exactly. I think mini demo = streaming + show one control, like caching or batching recommendation, or at least the token/latency breakdown page.

[02:52] Colin O'Donnell: For mini demo we can have a single script that does streaming call and then opens the saved dashboard. But we need it deterministic.

[03:01] Markus Klein: Let’s capture that as an action item. Renee, can you draft it.

[03:05] Renee Sullivan: Yep.

[03:07] Talia Benson: Noted.

[03:09] Markus Klein: Next: what broke live.

[03:12] Avery Johnson: 429 throttling. Twice in the last two weeks. Not in the demo tenant, but in a trial we spun up, and once in the tenant when I ran the same script back-to-back.

[03:23] Priyom Das: Yeah and it’s a bad look. The prospect hears “reliability” and then sees “rate limit exceeded.” Even if it’s our safety.

[03:31] Cole Summers (mentioned): I’m not on but this is quotas, right.

[03:34] Markus Klein: Cole’s not here but we’ll route it. What’s the fix you want?

[03:39] Avery Johnson: Give us more headroom by default for demos, and/or a pre-demo check that says “you’re about to hit limit.” Like a gas gauge.

[03:48] Isabelle Laurent: CRM-wise, if it’s prospect trial vs demo tenant, we should tag it. People are mixing.

[03:55] Talia Benson: Yeah that’s on scope: “when to use demo tenant vs spin up trial.”

[04:01] Priyom Das: Also, the current talk track doesn’t tell you what to do when you get a 429. People panic.

[04:08] Soojin Lee: We can add a sidebar: “If you see 429: explain quotas, switch to cached canned response, proceed to Console screenshot.”

[04:15] Markus Klein: I want a strict Plan B rule. Like, don’t debug live.

[04:20] Sean Gallagher: Please. From SRE perspective, live-debugging is how you end up screensharing internal dashboards with too much info.

[04:27] Camila Reyes: And it feels chaotic. The buyer loses trust.

[04:31] Markus Klein: Great. Plan B needs to be explicit.

[04:35] Simran Kaur: On determinism: the fallback scenario is currently dependent on, like, real capacity conditions. That’s inherently flaky. We need a deterministic trigger. For example, route policy that fails a canary on purpose, or a synthetic “capacity constrained” toggle in the tenant.

[04:52] Chloe Martin: We can do it with a routing rule that returns a controlled 5xx from a mock upstream? Or a “shadow route” that always errors.

[05:00] Colin O'Donnell: Yeah, like a route to a tiny stub service that always returns 503, to force fallback.

[05:06] Markus Klein: That would be perfect. So the “failure mode” is predictable and not scary.

[05:11] Simran Kaur: Exactly. And then we can narrate: “We inject a failure and show the platform stays online.”

[05:19] Priyom Das: That’s the moment that sells platform teams. When you show graceful degradation.

[05:24] Lukas Meyer: Also regulated teams. They want to see control.

[05:28] Markus Klein: Okay. Console clickpath issues. Chloe?

[05:32] Chloe Martin: I’ve watched a couple recordings. People get lost between Routes, Rollouts, and Policies. We renamed some things recently, and the deck screenshots are slightly out of date. Also the “Fallbacks” panel is not where people expect.

[05:48] Avery Johnson: Yeah I literally said “click on routing,” and there are like three nav items that look like routing. I choose wrong about 30% of the time.

[05:56] Soojin Lee: The talk track currently says “Routes → Fallbacks” and that’s not accurate.

[06:01] Chloe Martin: It’s Routes → Policy, then inside policy you see fallback targets. We can simplify in the UI, but short term I’ll make a 3 screenshot clickpath.

[06:14] Talia Benson: Action item for Chloe, got it.

[06:16] Markus Klein: Dashboard stability. Logan, you mentioned refresh. Anything else?

[06:22] Logan Wright: Some panels depend on a query that occasionally times out during load. When it does, it shows a blank chart. That reads as broken.

[06:30] Priyom Das: That happened on a call with a fintech. I was like “uh it’s loading.” Not great.

[06:36] Logan Wright: We can precompute the aggregates for the demo tenant to make it stable. Also reduce the query range by default (last 15 minutes, not last 24 hours).

[06:48] Markus Klein: Do it. Demo tenant should bias for speed and predictability.

[06:53] Stephanie Nguyen: Another break: model output variance. When we do “structured output” or tool calling, if the model chooses a different phrasing, the AE gets thrown because the expected output in the script doesn’t match.

[07:07] Renee Sullivan: Yeah. We need “expected shape” not “exact words,” and also we should set temperature to 0 and use a small prompt that’s been tested.

[07:17] Colin O'Donnell: Even at temp 0, some models can vary slightly if the backend changes. So we need canned outputs as Plan B.

[07:26] Soojin Lee: We should literally have a line: “LLMs are probabilistic; Redwood helps you measure and control; for demos we pin version and settings.” Then if output differs, it’s not a surprise.

[07:41] Avery Johnson: That framing helps. Right now if output is different it looks like we don’t know our own product.

[07:47] Markus Klein: What about Dedicated vs Private pivots? Are people using the branches?

[07:52] Priyom Das: I do, but it’s clunky. The deck has like two slides at the end. If they’re security-first, you need that earlier. They ask “SSO? audit logs? retention?” and we’re still talking about latency.

[08:06] Lukas Meyer: Agree. In EMEA, the question is “EU only?” and if we can’t answer quickly it derails. I’ve started saying: “Hosted is multi-region; Dedicated can be region pinned; Private is your VPC/on-prem.” Then continue.

[08:21] Camila Reyes: And from marketing, we need consistent wording on retention and logging. Don’t ad-lib.

[08:26] Sean Gallagher: Please don’t promise “no logs” broadly. It’s “demo tenant is sanitized and has safe logging.”

[08:33] Soojin Lee: I’ll align with Naomi’s FAQ language. We’ll add an “If asked” panel.

[08:40] Markus Klein: Competitive questions? Anyone getting “why not Bedrock” or “why not OpenAI”?

[08:46] Avery Johnson: Constantly. I say: “If you only need a model, sure. If you need serving control across environments, predictable costs, and observability, Redwood is the platform layer.”

[08:58] Priyom Das: I got Together and Replicate comparisons. Mostly price. I refuse to talk exact numbers.

[09:05] Camila Reyes: Correct. No pricing numbers in the deck. Use ranges and then “we’ll scope.”

[09:11] Stephanie Nguyen: People also ask “is this just vLLM.” We need a crisp answer: runtime + orchestration + tooling.

[09:18] Markus Klein: That should be in objections doc, but maybe also one sentence in talk track.

[09:22] Soojin Lee: Yup.

[09:24] Talia Benson: I’m going to jump us to “what to cut.” If you had to cut 5 minutes, what goes.

[09:30] Priyom Das: I would cut the second half of the console tour. Like, don’t click every tab. Pick 2 pages: Routes/Policy and Cost dashboard. The rest can be screenshots.

[09:41] Avery Johnson: Same. The clicky-click stuff is where you risk something being slow or different.

[09:48] Chloe Martin: I feel attacked, but yes. (laughs)

[09:51] Markus Klein: It’s about demo reliability, not product pride.

[09:55] Renee Sullivan: For mini demo, it’s basically: one API call, one console view, one reliability story.

[10:02] Soojin Lee: Okay, we’ll restructure: “show value early,” then optional deep dive.

[10:08] Lukas Meyer: Add explicit “choose your own adventure”: if platform team, do routing/fallback; if ML, do quality regression / prompt sets; if security, do Private + audit logs posture.

[10:20] Simran Kaur: We don’t have the quality regression demo fully yet. We can at least show “prompt set” and “expected outputs” document and mention eval hooks.

[10:29] Markus Klein: Keep it honest: show what exists.

[10:33] Camila Reyes: Yes. “What we show live” vs “what we claim.”

[10:38] Talia Benson: Any other recurring breakages?

[10:41] Avery Johnson: Streaming disconnects. It’s rare but terrifying because it happens mid-sentence. Even if it’s the prospect wifi, it looks like us.

[10:50] Colin O'Donnell: We can add a retry in the demo script. And we can have a non-streaming fallback command.

[10:56] Markus Klein: Great. Also have a screenshot of a completed streamed response.

[11:02] Sean Gallagher: And maybe a status page / indicator you can point to: “platform is healthy.” Not internal.

[11:09] Logan Wright: We can do a lightweight demo status page for the tenant. Green/amber/red.

[11:14] Markus Klein: Please.

[11:16] Isabelle Laurent: Also for internal process: When it breaks, how do AEs report it. Right now it’s random Slack threads.

[11:24] Talia Benson: We’ll route to a single intake: Jira or Linear, but for field maybe a form.

[11:29] Markus Klein: Probably a #demo-tenant channel + pinned link to runbook, plus an issue template.

[11:35] Soojin Lee: Okay, last section: next dry runs. Stephanie and Lukas, can we schedule one NA and one EMEA next week?

[11:44] Stephanie Nguyen: Yes, I’ll bring two AEs.

[11:47] Lukas Meyer: Same.

[11:49] Markus Klein: Cool. Before we end, I want each person to say the single best slide/moment and single worst.

[11:56] Avery Johnson: Best: cost dashboard with token-level breakdown. Worst: wandering around Console nav trying to find fallback.

[12:06] Priyom Das: Best: injecting failure and showing fallback keeps app working. Worst: 429 surprise.

[12:13] Camila Reyes: Best: “unified across hosted/dedicated/private” narrative. Worst: any time we talk numbers.

[12:20] Chloe Martin: Best: routes table overview. Worst: the policy page is too dense, sorry.

[12:26] Logan Wright: Best: trace view showing latency breakdown. Worst: blank chart when query times out.

[12:33] Sean Gallagher: Best: reliability story. Worst: live debugging.

[12:37] Soojin Lee: Best: the “why Redwood” framing. Worst: we bury the lead in the first five minutes.

[12:44] Markus Klein: Great. Talia, can you send notes + action items.

[12:48] Talia Benson: Yep, I’ll send a recap today.

[12:51] Markus Klein: Thanks all. Let’s make it boring and repeatable.

[12:56] (crosstalk)

[12:58] Renee Sullivan: I’ll ping with mini demo draft.

[13:00] Markus Klein: Awesome. Ending recording.

---
Note: Transcript ends early due to Fireflies auto-stop after the main discussion; remaining time in calendar was used for scheduling and sidebar Q&A.
